questions.question: Four bells begin to ring together respectively at intervals of 6, 7, 9, 12 seconds. After how many seconds will they ring together again?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The time after which all bells ring together is the LCM of their individual ringing intervals.

LCM of 6, 7, 9, and 12 = 252 seconds.

Since the bells ring together every 252 seconds, we check for 252 or its multiples in the options.

Next multiple = 252 × 2 = 504 seconds, which matches an option.

**∴ The correct answer is 504 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Intervals at which the four bells ring = 6, 7, 9, and 12 seconds.

**Concept Used:**

The bells will ring together again after a time that is exactly divisible by all the individual intervals. This specific time represents the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the given numbers. If the exact LCM is not among the options, any integer multiple of the LCM is a valid answer since the bells continue to ring together periodically.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factorization of 6 = 2 × 3

⇒ Prime factorization of 7 = 7

⇒ Prime factorization of 9 = 3²

⇒ Prime factorization of 12 = 2² × 3

⇒ LCM = Product of the highest powers of all present prime factors

⇒ LCM = 2² × 3² × 7

⇒ LCM = 4 × 9 × 7 = 252 seconds

⇒ This means the bells will ring together every 252 seconds (i.e., at 252s, 504s, 756s, etc.).

⇒ Analyzing the given options, we find that 504 is exactly divisible by 252 (252 × 2 = 504).

**∴ The correct answer is 504 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM for Periodic Events

For events that repeat at different regular intervals (like bells tolling, traffic lights changing, or runners on a circular track), they will all occur together again at exactly the LCM of their individual intervals.

Multiples of LCM

If the events coincide for the first time at the LCM, they will continue to simultaneously coincide at every successive integer multiple of the LCM (e.g., 2 × LCM, 3 × LCM).

HCF for Maximum Grouping

While LCM is for simultaneous forward occurrences, the Highest Common Factor (HCF) is used when dividing items into the largest possible equal groups without leaving any remainder (e.g., cutting ropes into maximum equal lengths).
</p

questions.question: The perimeter and area of a rectangular sheet are 40 m and 72 m², respectively. The length of the diagonal will be:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Sum of **length** and **width** (l + b) = **Perimeter** ÷ 2 = 40 ÷ 2 = 20 m.

**Area** (l × b) = 72 m².

Relationship: **Diagonal**² = (l + b)² − 2(l × b).

Diagonal² = 20² − 2 × 72 = 400 − 144 = 256.

Diagonal = √256 = 16 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 m.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Perimeter** of the **rectangular sheet** = 40 m

**Area** of the **rectangular sheet** = 72 m²

**Formula Used:**

1. Perimeter = 2(Length + Breadth)

2. Area = Length × Breadth

3. Diagonal (d) = √(Length² + Breadth²)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/db5695b8b47941a56f94bd2af92bf6bd775801e30e0eb80d65f30e81ce22ffdd.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2(l + b) = 40

⇒ l + b = 20 m

⇒ l × b = 72 m²

We know that (l + b)² = l² + b² + 2lb

⇒ 20² = l² + b² + 2(72)

⇒ 400 = l² + b² + 144

⇒ l² + b² = 400 − 144

⇒ l² + b² = 256

⇒ Diagonal (d) = √(l² + b²) = √256

⇒ d = 16 m

**∴ The correct answer is 16 m.**

**__Additional Information__**

Pythagoras Theorem in Rectangle

A rectangle is divided into two right-angled triangles by its diagonal. Thus, d² = l² + b².

Direct Relation Formula

The diagonal can be directly found if perimeter (P) and area (A) are known: d = √[(P/2)² − 2A].

Rectangle Diagonals

In a rectangle, both diagonals are **equal in length** and **bisect** each other.</p

questions.question: If the radius of sphere is decreased by 80 percent, then volume of sphere will be decreased by what percentage?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Radius ratio** (Initial : New) = 100 : (100 − 80) = 100 : 20 = 5 : 1.

Since **Volume** of a sphere is proportional to the **cube** of its radius (V ∝ r³):

**Volume ratio** = 5³ : 1³ = 125 : 1.

Reduction in volume = 125 − 1 = 124 units.

Percentage decrease = (Decrease ÷ Initial Volume) × 100 = (124 ÷ 125) × 100 = 99.2%.

**∴ The correct answer is 99.2 percent.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The **radius** of the sphere is decreased by 80%.

**Formula Used:** Volume of a **Sphere** = (4/3) × π × r³

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fefba45a673c4911baf4195529de89d7799ff0973698aa0cc076bce8ddd132a7.png] 

⇒ Let the initial **radius** (r₁) = 10 units.

⇒ Initial **Volume** (V₁) = (4/3) × π × (10)³ = (4000/3) π cubic units.

⇒ New radius (r₂) = 10 − (80% of 10) = 10 − 8 = 2 units.

⇒ New **Volume** (V₂) = (4/3) × π × (2)³ = (32/3) π cubic units.

⇒ Decrease in Volume = V₁ − V₂ = (4000/3) π − (32/3) π = (3968/3) π cubic units.

⇒ Percentage Decrease = [(3968/3) π ÷ (4000/3) π] × 100

⇒ Percentage Decrease = (3968 ÷ 4000) × 100 = 0.992 × 100 = 99.2%.

**∴ The correct answer is 99.2 percent.**

**__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Sphere

The amount of space occupied by a 3D sphere is given by V = (4/3)πr³, where r is the **radius**.

Surface Area of a Sphere

The total **surface area** of a sphere is given by A = 4πr². If radius decreases by 80%, area decreases by 96%.

Successive Percentage Rule

For volume changes, the percentage change can be calculated using successive effective rates three times: x + y + (xy/100).

Ratio and Powers

If a linear dimension changes by ratio a:b, then **Area** changes by a²:b² and **Volume** changes by a³:b³.</p

questions.question: The curved surface area of a cylindrical pillar is 528 m² and its volume is 1848 m³ . The ratio between its radius and height is ________.

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Curved Surface Area (CSA)** of the pillar = 528 m²

**Volume (V)** of the pillar = 1848 m³

⇒ 44 × h = 528

⇒ **Height (h)** = 528 ÷ 44 = 12 m

Ratio of Radius (r) to Height (h):

⇒ r : h = 7 : 12

**∴ The correct answer is 7 : 12.**

**__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area (TSA) of a Cylinder

The total surface area includes the curved surface and the two circular ends: TSA = 2πr(r + h).

Volume of a Cone

For a cone with the same radius and height as a cylinder, its volume is one-third of the cylinder: V = (1/3)πr²h.

Relationship between r, h, V and CSA

questions.question: ​A dishonest shopkeeper sells mangoes at Rs. 30/kg bought at Rs. 20/kg and he is giving 800 g instead of 1 kg. The shopkeeper's actual profit percentage is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Price ratio (CP : SP) = 20 : 30 = 2 : 3

Weight ratio (Actual : Claimed) = 800 : 1000 = 4 : 5

Effective CP : SP ratio = (2 × 4) : (3 × 5) = 8 : 15

Profit = 15 − 8 = 7 units.

Profit % = (7 ÷ 8) × 100 = 87.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 87.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost price of 1 kg (1000 g) mangoes = Rs. 20

Selling price of 1 kg mangoes = Rs. 30

Actual weight given instead of 1 kg = 800 g

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b0264c8255e9fb433aac2ba0121258579f1c91b8a8619c98277adb50b3e9924c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Cost price of 1 g mango = 20 ÷ 1000 = Rs. 0.02

⇒ Actual cost price of 800 g mangoes = 800 × 0.02 = Rs. 16

⇒ The shopkeeper charges Rs. 30 for 800 g (claiming it as 1 kg).

⇒ Actual Selling price = Rs. 30

⇒ Profit = SP − Actual CP

⇒ Profit = 30 − 16 = Rs. 14

⇒ Profit % = (Profit ÷ Actual CP) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (14 ÷ 16) × 100 = 87.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 87.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Dishonest Dealer Concept

When a dealer sells goods using false weights, the actual cost price is based on the true weight delivered to the customer, while the selling price is based on the claimed weight.

Successive Ratio Method

The overall profit ratio can be derived by multiplying the individual price markup ratio (CP : SP) by the cheating weight ratio (Actual Weight : Claimed Weight).

Profit % Formula

questions.question: If sec θ - cos θ = 14 and 14 sec θ = x, then the value of x is _________.
questions.solution:

Given: 14 = **sec θ − cos θ**

Substitute 14 in the second equation: x = (**sec θ − cos θ**) × **sec θ**

⇒ x = sec² θ − (cos θ × sec θ)

⇒ x = sec² θ − 1 = tan² θ

**∴ The correct answer is tan² θ.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ Substitute the value of 14 in the second equation: x = (sec θ − cos θ) × sec θ

⇒ x = sec² θ − (cos θ × sec θ)

⇒ Since cos θ × sec θ = 1, we get x = sec² θ − 1

⇒ Using identity sec² θ − tan² θ = 1, x = tan² θ

**∴ The correct answer is tan² θ.**

Fundamental square relations: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ, and 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.

questions.question: A cone of height 22 cm and diameter 20 cm is mounted on a hemisphere of the same diameter. Find the volume of the solid formed.

Total Volume = Volume of Cone + Volume of Hemisphere

V = (1/3) × π × r² × (h + 2r)

Substitute radius r = 10 cm and height h = 22 cm:

V = (1/3) × (22/7) × 100 × (22 + 20) = (2200 / 21) × 42 = 4400 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 4400 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Formula Used:**

Volume of Cone = (1/3) × π × r² × h

Volume of Hemisphere = (2/3) × π × r³

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Volume = [(1/3) × π × r² × h] + [(2/3) × π × r³]

⇒ Total Volume = (1/3) × π × r² × (h + 2r)

⇒ Total Volume = (1/3) × (22/7) × (10)² × (22 + 2 × 10)

⇒ Total Volume = (1/3) × (22/7) × 100 × (22 + 20)

⇒ Total Volume = (1/3) × (22/7) × 100 × 42

⇒ Total Volume = 2200 × (42 / 21)

⇒ Total Volume = 2200 × 2 = 4400 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 4400 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of Cylinder

A cylinder's volume is V = π × r² × h. A cone is exactly one-third the volume of a cylinder with the exact same base and height.

Surface Area of Cone

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = π × r × l, where slant height l = √(r² + h²). Total Surface Area = π × r × (r + l).

Surface Area of Hemisphere

Curved Surface Area = 2 × π × r². Total Surface Area (including the flat circular base) = 3 × π × r².

questions.solution:

The number of **diagonals** in a polygon with **n** sides is given by the formula: **n(n − 3) ÷ 2**.

For a polygon with **5 sides** (a **pentagon**), substitute n = 5.

Number of diagonals = 5 × (5 − 3) ÷ 2 = 5 × 2 ÷ 2 = 5.

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of sides of the regular polygon (**n**) = 5

A diagonal is a line segment connecting two **non-adjacent vertices**. The total number of ways to connect any two vertices is ⁿC₂, which includes both sides and diagonals.

⇒ ⁵C₂ = (5 × 4) ÷ (2 × 1) = 10

⇒ Number of diagonals = 10 − (Number of sides)

⇒ Number of diagonals = 10 − 5 = 5

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

**__Additional Information__**

Sum of Interior Angles

The sum of all interior angles of a polygon with **n** sides is (n − 2) × 180°.

Each Interior Angle (Regular Polygon)

Exterior Angles

questions.question: A sum become (61)/(60) of itself in 2 months at simple interest. Find the rate at which the sum is invested.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__
Let the **Principal** be 60 units. The **Amount** becomes 61 units.

**Simple Interest** for **2 months** = 61 − 60 = 1 unit.

Interest for 12 months (1 year) = 1 × 6 = 6 units.

**Rate of interest** per annum = (Interest per year ÷ Principal) × 100 = (6 ÷ 60) × 100 = 10%.

**∴ The correct answer is 10% p.a.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Amount** (A) = 61/60 of **Principal** (P)

**Time** (T) = 2 months = 2/12 = 1/6 year

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount (A) = P + SI
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c0ea4fab6d98b539e611840ed1fc8149d081a9466bbb6ae3777debb39230ea6c.png] 
**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = (61/60)P − P = (1/60)P

⇒ (1/60)P = (P × R × 1/6) ÷ 100

⇒ 1/60 = (R/6) ÷ 100

⇒ 1/60 = R ÷ 600

⇒ R = 600 ÷ 60

⇒ R = 10%

**∴ The correct answer is 10% p.a.**

**__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Formula

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100, where P is principal, R is rate per annum, and T is time in years.

Time Conversion

Always convert time into years: T (years) = Time in months ÷ 12.

Amount and Interest Relation

Amount (A) = Principal (P) + Simple Interest (SI). Also, A = P(1 + RT/100).</p

• ASCII uses a **7-bit binary code** to represent characters, allowing it to encode **128 unique characters**. These include letters (both uppercase and lowercase), digits, punctuation marks, control characters, and some special symbols.
 
• It was first developed in the **1960s** and became a widely accepted standard, especially in early computer systems and networks.
 
• ASCII serves as a foundation for many modern character encoding systems, such as **Unicode**, which extends ASCII to include characters from multiple languages and scripts. *Hence, ASCII remains a critical component in computing.*
 
• ASCII is used primarily to represent English characters and symbols, making it less suitable for languages with larger character sets. However, it remains relevant for basic text representation and communication protocols. *Hence, this explanation validates the importance of ASCII.*

questions.question: The term **“**Langmuir Effect”, often mentioned in the news, refers to which one of the following?

options.text: The upward movement of moist air due to orographic lifting over mountainous regions
The coalescence of water droplets in clouds until they become heavy enough to overcome updrafts and fall as intense rainfall
The interaction between ocean currents and wind that leads to wave formation
The process of heat transfer from the Earth's surface to the upper atmosphere through radiation

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option B**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The core concept in this question is the **Langmuir Effect in the context of cloudbursts**, where cloud droplets grow by coalescence and eventually fall as sudden intense rainfall. This is also referred to as the **Langmuir precipitation process** in cloudburst-related discussions.
 
• **Option A: **This describes **orographic lifting**, where moist air rises over mountains, cools and condenses. It is an important condition for rainfall in hilly regions, but it is not the Langmuir Effect. Hence, **Option A is incorrect. **
 
• **Option B: **The Langmuir Effect refers to the coalescence of smaller water droplets into larger droplets within clouds. These droplets continue to grow until their weight becomes sufficient to overcome the upward air currents, leading to sudden and intense precipitation. Hence, **Option B is correct. **
 
• **Option C: **This is related to oceanic processes and should not be confused with the cloudburst-related Langmuir precipitation process. In this question, the context is intense rainfall, not ocean circulation. Hence, **Option C is incorrect. **
 
• **Option D: **This refers to radiative heat transfer and has no direct connection with cloudburst formation or droplet coalescence. Hence, **Option D is incorrect. **
 
• Therefore, **Option B correctly explains the Langmuir Effect in the cloudburst context. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A **cloudburst** is an extremely intense rainfall event over a small area. In the Indian context, it is generally associated with rainfall of about **100 mm or more within one hour** over a localized region. Such events can trigger flash floods, landslides and mudflows, especially in hilly regions.
 
• Cloudbursts usually occur under conditions of **high humidity, unstable atmosphere, strong updrafts, orographic lifting and moisture-laden winds**. Cumulonimbus clouds play an important role in such events.
 
• The **Langmuir precipitation process** helps explain how water droplets inside clouds rapidly grow by merging with smaller droplets. Once the droplets become too heavy to remain suspended, they fall suddenly as intense rainfall.
 
• Major hazards associated with cloudbursts include **flash floods, landslides, mudflows, damage to infrastructure, river course changes and loss of life**, particularly in the Himalayan and other mountainous regions.

questions.question: The term “Grasshopper Effect”, often mentioned in the context of pollution in the Arctic region, refers to which one of the following?

options.text: The rapid movement of marine species from tropical to polar regions due to climate change
The long-range transport of pollutants through repeated cycles of evaporation and condensation, leading to their accumulation in colder regions
The deposition of pollutants directly into polar regions due to local industrial activities
The biological magnification of toxins across trophic levels in Arctic food chains

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option B**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The core concept in this question is the **Grasshopper Effect**, also known as **Global Distillation**. It explains how certain pollutants travel long distances and accumulate in colder regions such as the Arctic.
 
• **Option A: **This refers to the movement of species due to climate change. It does not explain the long-range transport of pollutants. Hence, **Option A is incorrect. **
 
• **Option B:**The Grasshopper Effect refers to the long-range movement of volatile pollutants through repeated cycles of evaporation and condensation. Pollutants evaporate in warmer regions, move through atmospheric currents, condense in cooler regions and gradually accumulate in cold areas such as the Arctic. Hence, **Option B is correct. **
 
• **Option C:**This refers to pollution caused by local industrial activities. The Grasshopper Effect mainly explains the transport of pollutants from distant regions to remote cold regions. Hence, **Option C is incorrect. **
 
• **Option D: **This describes **biomagnification**, where toxins increase in concentration across trophic levels in a food chain. It is different from the Grasshopper Effect. Hence, **Option D is incorrect. **
 
• Therefore, **Option B is the correct answer. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Grasshopper Effect** is also called **Global Distillation**. It explains why pollutants released in industrial and agricultural regions can be found in remote polar areas.
 
• In this process, pollutants evaporate in warm regions, travel through the atmosphere, condense in cooler regions and may re-evaporate again. Through repeated cycles, they move progressively toward colder regions.
 
• The Arctic is especially vulnerable because low temperatures reduce re-evaporation. As a result, it acts as a **global sink** for certain pollutants.
 
• Pollutants associated with this process include **Persistent Organic Pollutants (POPs)**, pesticides, industrial chemicals and other long-lasting toxic substances.
 
• The major impacts include bioaccumulation in Arctic food chains, risks to indigenous communities dependent on traditional food sources, and disruption of fragile polar ecosystems.

The Correct answer is __**Charles Babbage**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Charles Babbage**, often referred to as the “Father of the Computer,” designed the **Analytical Engine**, which is considered the first fully automatic calculating machine.
 
• The Analytical Engine was conceptualized in the mid-19th century and was a mechanical general-purpose computer.
 
• It was designed to perform **arithmetic operations** automatically and could be programmed using punched cards, a concept later adopted by early computers.
 
• The machine included key components such as the **mill (analogous to the CPU)**, the **store (memory)**, and mechanisms for input/output.
 
• Charles Babbage's innovations laid the groundwork for modern computing, although the Analytical Engine was never fully constructed during his lifetime due to **technological limitations**.
 
• Babbage collaborated with **Ada Lovelace**, who is considered the first computer programmer for creating algorithms intended to run on the Analytical Engine.
 
• The Analytical Engine was a significant development in the history of computing, marking the transition from manual calculation to automated computing systems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Blaise Pascal**__

 __
 
• **Blaise Pascal** was a French mathematician, physicist, and inventor who developed the **Pascaline**, one of the first mechanical calculators, in the 17th century.
 
• Pascal’s invention was primarily designed to assist in addition and subtraction and was not programmable like Babbage's Analytical Engine.
 
• The Pascaline was manually operated and used a series of gears and dials.
 
• Pascal’s contributions were foundational in the field of mechanical computation but did not extend to general-purpose computing.
 
 
 
• **Leibniz**__
 __
 
• **Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz**, a German mathematician and philosopher, improved upon Pascal’s ideas and developed the **Stepped Reckoner**, a mechanical calculator capable of performing addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division.
 
• Leibniz is also credited with developing the **binary number system**, which is fundamental to modern computing.
 
• While his work advanced mechanical computation, it did not achieve the level of automation or programmability envisioned by Babbage.
 
 
 
• **John Von Neumann**__
 
 
• **John Von Neumann** was a 20th-century mathematician and physicist who contributed significantly to the development of modern computer architecture.
 
• He proposed the concept of the **stored-program architecture**, which is used in almost all modern computers.
 
• Von Neumann’s work came much later than Babbage’s and focused on electronic computing rather than mechanical systems.
 
• The architecture he developed is known as the **Von Neumann architecture**, which forms the basis of most computer designs today.

questions.question: In a class, Raju ranked sixteenth from the top and forty-ninth from the bottom among those who passed an examination. Seven students did not appear in the examination and two failed. What is the total number of students in the class?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Raju ranked sixteenth from the top and forty-ninth from the bottom among those who passed an examination

Total number of students who passed the examination = 16 + 49 - 1 = 65 -1 = 64

Seven students did not appear in the examination and two failed.

Therefore, the total number of students in the class = 64 + 7 + 2 = 73

Hence, the correct answer is __**73**__.

questions.question: During photosynthesis the oxygen in glucose comes from ______.

options.text: Both from water and carbon dioxide

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Carbon dioxide**__**.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• Photosynthesis is the physiochemical process, in which carbohydrates (organic compounds) are formed from inorganic substrates like H₂O & CO₂ in the presence of light and pigments.
 
• O₂ is evolved as a by-product during photosynthesis.
 
• The **oxygen molecule present in glucose is derived from carbon dioxide** during **Calvin cycle of photosynthesis**.
 
• The CO₂ molecule is first added to 3-phosphoglycerate during the carboxylation reaction of Calvin cycle, and is later used to form glucose.
 
• While molecular oxygen that is liberated during photosynthesis is produced from photolysis of water during the light reaction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Photosynthesis can be simply divided into 4 major processes

 
• Absorption of light energy by **Chlorophyll pigment.**
 
• Conversion of light energy into chemical energy.
 
• **Splitting of water or Photolysis** during Non-cyclic photophosphorylation.

** H₂O → 2H⁺ + 2e⁻⁻ + [IMAGE: file:///C:/Users/utkar/AppData/Local/Temp/OICE_7537A668-6D1D-4E05-8EA6-84C3B2569657.0/msohtmlclip1/01/clip_image004.png] O₂ **↑

**The oxygen that evolved during this process comes from water__**.

 
• **Reduction of CO₂ to carbohydrates (Glucose) during Dark reaction.**

**​**The CO2 undergoes reduction and its O2 is utilized in the formation of Glucose.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **__Mistake Points__**

The **O₂ released during photolysis is the evolved O₂**, whereas **the O₂ released during the reduction of CO₂ is the O₂ in glucose.**
